extracted.intended_audience: funding agencies, academic institutions, journals/publishers, organizations that supply metrics, and individual researchers (including those serving on hiring/tenure/funding committees)
extracted.subtask_description: High-level, cross-disciplinary recommendations for how research outputs and researchers should be evaluated, aimed at changing assessment practices used by funders, institutions, publishers, metric-providers, and researchers themselves. Focuses on reducing reliance on journal-based metrics and broadening consideration of research outputs and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use journal-based metrics as surrogate measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use journal-based metrics, such as Journal Impact Factors, as a surrogate measure of the quality of individual research articles, to assess an individual scientist’s contributions, or in hiring, promotion, or funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Journal Impact Factor (JIF) was created to help librarians choose journals, not to measure article quality. Known limitations include: (A) citation distributions within journals are highly skewed; (B) JIF properties are field-specific and composite across diverse article types (primary papers, reviews); (C) JIFs can be manipulated by editorial policy; (D) data used to calculate JIFs are not transparent or openly available. The recommendation is a general prohibition on using journal-level metrics as substitutes for article- or researcher-level assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about evaluation criteria (funders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding agencies should be explicit about the criteria used in evaluating the scientific productivity of grant applicants and clearly highlight, especially for early-stage investigators, that the scientific content of a paper is much more important than publication metrics or the identity of the journal in which it was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance emphasizes transparency of criteria and prioritizing scientific content over metrics or journal reputation when assessing applicants, with special attention to early-career researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider all research outputs and broad impact measures (funders)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of research assessment, consider the value and impact of all research outputs (including datasets and software) in addition to research publications, and consider a broad range of impact measures including qualitative indicators of research impact, such as influence on policy and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages funders to value non-article outputs (data, software, reagents, trained personnel, IP) and to include qualitative indicators (policy influence, practice change) alongside quantitative measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about criteria for hiring/tenure/promotion (institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions should be explicit about the criteria used to reach hiring, tenure, and promotion decisions, clearly highlighting, especially for early-stage investigators, that the scientific content of a paper is much more important than publication metrics or the identity of the journal in which it was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors the guidance for funders: institutional decision processes should be transparent and prioritize content over journal-based indicators; address early-stage investigators explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider all research outputs and broad impact measures (institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of research assessment, consider the value and impact of all research outputs (including datasets and software) in addition to research publications, and consider a broad range of impact measures including qualitative indicators of research impact, such as influence on policy and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should expand recognized outputs beyond publications, and incorporate qualitative and alternative impact measures when assessing researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce emphasis on Journal Impact Factor in publisher promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Greatly reduce emphasis on the journal impact factor as a promotional tool, ideally by ceasing to promote the impact factor or by presenting the metric in the context of a variety of journal-based metrics (e.g., 5-year impact factor, EigenFactor, SCImago, h-index, editorial and publication times, etc.) that provide a richer view of journal performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should stop using JIF as the primary promotional statistic; if metrics are shown, present multiple complementary metrics to give a fuller picture and avoid over-reliance on a single indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide article-level metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Make available a range of article-level metrics to encourage a shift toward assessment based on the scientific content of an article rather than publication metrics of the journal in which it was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should publish per-article indicators (citations, downloads, altmetrics, usage, etc.) so assessments can focus on article-specific impact rather than journal averages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage responsible authorship and contribution transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage responsible authorship practices and the provision of information about the specific contributions of each author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should require or encourage author contribution statements, clarify authorship criteria, and foster accountability for who did what in the research and writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove reuse limitations on reference lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a journal is open-access or subscription-based, remove all reuse limitations on reference lists in research articles and make them available under the Creative Commons Public Domain Dedication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference lists should be openly reusable to enable computational and other downstream uses; publishers should not restrict reuse of bibliographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove or reduce constraints on number of references; favor primary literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove or reduce the constraints on the number of references in research articles, and, where appropriate, mandate the citation of primary literature in favor of reviews in order to give credit to the group(s) who first reported a finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should avoid arbitrary limits on references that can impede proper attribution; when relevant, require citing original discoveries rather than reviews to allocate credit fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be open and transparent about metric data and methods (metric providers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be open and transparent by providing data and methods used to calculate all metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations supplying metrics should publish the datasets and algorithms behind metrics so users can assess validity, reproduce calculations, and detect biases or errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide data under an unrestricted licence and computational access (metric providers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the data under a licence that allows unrestricted reuse, and provide computational access to data, where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metric providers should ensure data are legally reusable (e.g., permissive licence) and technically accessible (APIs, bulk downloads) to enable independent analysis and tool development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and counter inappropriate manipulation of metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Be clear that inappropriate manipulation of metrics will not be tolerated; be explicit about what constitutes inappropriate manipulation and what measures will be taken to combat this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metric organizations and journals should define gaming/manipulation behaviors (e.g., coerced citations, editorial tactics) and state enforcement or remediation policies to preserve metric integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for variation in article types and subject areas when using metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for the variation in article types (e.g., reviews versus research articles), and in different subject areas when metrics are used, aggregated, or compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying metrics for comparison or aggregation, adjust for differences between article types and disciplinary citation practices to avoid misleading comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess based on scientific content in committee decisions (researchers serving on committees)
rubrics_metrics.description: When involved in committees making decisions about funding, hiring, tenure, or promotion, make assessments based on scientific content rather than publication metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers serving as evaluators should prioritize reading and judging the work itself (quality, rigor, significance) rather than relying on journal reputation or impact factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite primary literature where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever appropriate, cite primary literature in which observations are first reported rather than reviews in order to give credit where credit is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should favor original sources when acknowledging discoveries so credit accrues to the correct groups; this practice also supports accurate attribution in assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a range of article metrics and indicators in personal/supporting statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a range of article metrics and indicators on personal/supporting statements, as evidence of the impact of individual published articles and other research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and reviewers should present multiple article-level indicators and contextual information (e.g., statements of influence, policy impact) to demonstrate impact beyond journal-level metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge inappropriate reliance on Journal Impact Factors and teach best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenge research assessment practices that rely inappropriately on Journal Impact Factors and promote and teach best practice that focuses on the value and influence of specific research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should actively advocate for reform in assessment practices, educate peers and committees about the limitations of journal-based metrics, and promote approaches that evaluate specific outputs and diverse impacts.
